headline: Sales accelerate; a one-time tax benefit flatters earnings
summary_short: QSR's Q1 FY2026 revenue was $2,264M (+7.3% y/y, -8.2% q/q vs. a seasonally larger Q4), as system-wide sales growth accelerated to 6.2% led by an 11.1% constant-currency gain at International; net income jumped to $338M as a discrete tax benefit cut the effective tax rate to 7.9% from 26.9% a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue rose 7.3% y/y (-8.2% q/q) to $2,264M on higher supply-chain sales and system-wide sales growth across INTL (+11.1%), BK (+5.5%), TH (+2.4%) and FHS (+7.2%); PLK was the outlier, with system-wide sales down 3.9% and US comparable sales down 6.5%. Operating income grew 39.3% y/y on a foreign-exchange gain (versus a loss a year ago) and higher segment income, while G&A fell on lower compensation costs. Net income surged 112.6% y/y to $338M, helped by the effective tax rate falling to 7.9% from 26.9% on a discrete deferred-tax benefit from an intra-group reorganization; another ~$170M benefit is due in Q2. Cash fell to $1,012M (-13.0% q/q) after $283M of dividends and buybacks; long-term debt was flat at $13,268M.

drivers.explanation: System-wide sales growth accelerated to 6.2% (INTL +11.1%, BK +5.5%), but most of net income's y/y jump came from a discrete tax benefit tied to an intra-group reorganization, not operating performance.
Higher Supply chain sales and system-wide sales growth across the INTL, BK, TH and FHS franchisor segments, plus a favorable FX impact.
Primarily a net gain on foreign-denominated intercompany remeasurement (versus a loss a year ago) plus higher segment income across INTL, BK, TH and FHS.
Increase in Income from operations plus a discrete tax benefit that cut the effective tax rate to 7.9% from 26.9%, from revaluing deferred tax liabilities in an intra-group reorganization.
Higher segment income across INTL, BK, TH and FHS, plus lower income tax and interest payments than a year ago.
The y/y decline in debt (and resulting lower interest expense) mainly reflects a voluntary partial repayment of Term Loan B made during 2025.
Financing activities used $306M, primarily share repurchases and an increase in dividend payments, more than offsetting the $227M generated by operations.

confidence_notes: REGENERATION (force-regen run): this file overwrites any prior summary for this period. eps_diluted_usd and eps_usd q/q comparisons use the shard's Q4 FY2025 prior values, which are Yahoo-sourced (pre-SEC-rederive) while the Q1 FY2026 actuals are SEC-verbatim; the two are not surprise pairs so the same-basis rule doesn't gate them, but the q/q jump (EPS $0.34→$0.97) is largely a real effect of Q4 2025 carrying a much higher 26.9%-plus effective tax rate and RH/BK China transaction costs versus Q1 2026's discrete tax benefit, not a data artifact. Effective tax rate fell to 7.9% (from 26.9% y/y) on a discrete benefit from revaluing deferred tax liabilities in an intra-group reorganization completed during the quarter; a further ~$170M discrete benefit is expected in the quarter ending June 30, 2026, and both reorganizations are expected to favorably affect the full-year rate. No formal revenue/EPS guidance range was given for FY2026 Q2 or full-year FY2026 in this filing; two other forward-looking company figures were captured onto the event's guidance array instead: the ~$170M Q2 discrete tax benefit, and the previously-disclosed 'Reclaim the Flame' plan (up to $700M through year-end 2028, of which the $550M Royal Reset tranche has $189M funded through Q1 FY2026).
